title: The local engine still passes --lowvram; the Pod dropped it on measurement (inert today under aimdo)
description: Opened as a speed hypothesis and DISPROVEN in the same session, at zero generation cost. --lowvram is inert on the engine we ship: ComfyUI 0.30.0 + torch 2.13 + comfy_aimdo 0.4.11 means dynamic VRAM is on, and model_management.py puts LOW_VRAM and NORMAL_VRAM in the SAME branch with the SAME budget (L983); no other vram_state branch tells them apart. Upstream's own docstring: it does nothing if dynamic vram is enabled. So the 11.5/16-dedicated-with-23.7-shared split is aimdo's JIT fault-in, not the flag, and the app-vs-bench gap is settings - the app's own log spans 6.4 to 143 s/it in one evening on one engine. WHAT SURVIVES is an engine half-wire: the Pod dropped the flag deliberately (MPI-146/156, start.sh VRAM_MODE empty) and the local engine never followed. It has sat in routes/comfy.js since the init commit 2026-03-31, predating every shipped model, so no measurement produced it - MPI-144 then copied it OUTWARD to the Pod to match the local engine. Costs nothing today; reactivates into MPI-156's 6-minute cold loads if a future engine ships torch below 2.8. NOT a blind deletion: model_management.py L122/L549 make the flag load-bearing on DirectML. Also records two user corrections the earlier draft had wrong - we DID ship a Q8_0 GGUF (MPI-168) and it OOM'd in ComfyUI-GGUF's dequant outside aimdo's fence (MPI-185, reverted by MPI-190), and offload is proven load-bearing (disabling aimdo container-OOM-killed a 4090 live).
